findings.text: — the done-when says "the existing `tests/test_a_lift_survives_reset_jitter.py` still passes", but the deliverable replaces the measured-jitter tolerance, and that test asserts the exact behaviour

findings.reason: the done-when must state that each reading reaches `end_cause`/`lift_watch.sweep` in its own call as `published_readings` returns a one-element list (reckon/crew/budget_lift.py:219), otherwise a node that takes "alternating" literally writes a test whose positive case and control both measure nothing.
findings.text: the done-when's positive case feeds "Readings alternating between that stamp and 04:59:38" and asserts they leave the lift in force, and the negative control restores the measured-jitter threshold and asserts "the 82-second drift must then end the lift"; but the jitter is the spread the history carries, so the two halves pull against the sequence length. Reproduced against the worktree: with a single drifted reading `_reset_observed` is True and with two readings `[04:58:15, 04:59:38]` it is True (history holds only the old stamp, jitter 1 s), but with four alternating readings `[04:58:15, 04:59:38, 04:58:15, 04:59:38]` it is False, because the history now carries the drifted stamp and the measured jitter is 83 s, which already exceeds the 82-second move. If the node builds the "alternating" sequence as one list of more than two readings, the unfixed code already leaves the lift in force (the positive assertion passes on code the fix never touched) and the restored-jitter control does not redden (the reason the control exists is lost).
